recipes.name: Bengali aloo chachchari
instructions: Peel the raw potatoes and cut them into uniform small cubes, then rinse thoroughly in water.
Slit the green chillies down the middle and set them aside.
In a pan, add the cubed potatoes and dry-sauté them on a medium flame for two minutes.
Add the slit green chillies into the pan with the potatoes and stir briefly.
Pour one and a half cups of water into the pan, ensuring the potatoes are mostly submerged.
Bring the water to a rolling boil, then turn the heat down to low.
Cover the pan tightly with a lid and simmer for twelve minutes until the potatoes are completely fork-tender.
Uncover the pan, mash a few potato cubes against the side with your ladle to thicken the light gravy, and serve.

recipes.name: Bengali Niramish aloor dum
instructions: Boil the potatoes until cooked but firm, peel them, and cut into large, uniform halves.
Finely chop the raw tomato, green chilli, and fresh coriander leaves.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, add the chopped tomatoes and cook on medium heat until they break down and turn mushy.
Add the chopped green chilli to the tomato paste and sauté for one minute.
Add the boiled potato pieces to the pan and toss gently to coat them with the tomato base.
Pour half a cup of water into the pan, cover with a lid, and let it simmer on low flame for five minutes.
Uncover the pan and allow the excess moisture to evaporate until a thick sauce clings to the potatoes.
Turn off the heat, garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves, and mix gently before serving.

recipes.name: Sada aloo chorchori
instructions: Wash the potatoes thoroughly, peel them, and slice into thin, small matchstick-like strips.
Place the sliced potato strips in a bowl of clean water to remove excess starch, then drain well.
In a non-stick frying pan, add the potato strips and the broken green chilli pieces.
Dry-sauté the potatoes over medium heat for about three minutes until they warm through completely.
Pour one cup of water into the pan and stir gently to mix with the potatoes and chillies.
Cover the frying pan securely with a lid and turn the heat down to low.
Simmer for ten minutes until the potato strips are perfectly soft and the water has reduced.
Remove the lid, stir to ensure the curry is moist but not watery, and remove from heat.

recipes.name: Moong dal khichuri
instructions: Put the dry moong dal into a pot and dry-roast it over medium flame until it turns aromatic and golden brown.
Remove the roasted dal, wash it thoroughly along with the basmati rice, and drain the water completely.
Peel the raw potato and slice it cleanly into two large, equal pieces.
In a deep cooking pot, combine the washed rice, roasted dal, and the potato halves.
Pour four katori of water into the pot and stir the mixture together once.
Bring the pot to a rolling boil over a high flame on your stovetop.
Lower the heat to low, cover the pot with a heavy lid, and let it cook slowly for twenty minutes.
Check that the rice and dal are completely mushy and integrated, then turn off the heat and serve hot.

recipes.name: Aloo bhate bhat
instructions: Wash the basmati rice in clean water multiple times until the water runs clear, then drain.
Peel the raw potato and keep it whole so it does not dissolve completely during boiling.
In a large deep pot, add the drained rice, the whole potato, and three cups of fresh water.
Place the pot over medium-high heat and bring the water to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot with a lid, and cook for fifteen minutes until the rice is done and the potato is fully soft.
Carefully scoop out the boiled potato from the hot rice and transfer it into a clean mixing bowl.
Add the finely chopped raw onion and green chilli to the bowl with the hot boiled potato.
Mash the potato thoroughly with a fork or spoon while incorporating the chopped onions and chillies, then serve alongside the hot rice.
